one-runner-per-tick.name: One runner per tick
one-runner-per-tick.statement: N copies of a scheduler share one schedule, so something must pick exactly one runner per tick.

dead-holder-blocks-forever.name: A dead holder blocks forever
dead-holder-blocks-forever.statement: A lock with no expiry outlives a crashed holder and blocks everyone, forever.

lock-ttl.name: TTL sets recovery time
lock-ttl.statement: A TTL bounds how long a dead holder can block; it is the crash-recovery time.

lease-renewal.name: Lease renewal
lease-renewal.statement: A long job keeps a short TTL by renewing while alive; renewing at TTL/2 leaves one retry of margin before expiry.

ttl-vs-renewal-interval.name: TTL and renewal interval are separate knobs
ttl-vs-renewal-interval.statement: TTL sets recovery time; the renewal interval trades safety margin against coordination overhead.
ttl-vs-renewal-interval.statement_learner: renew infinitely fast and you'd still wait the full TTL after a kill — to recover faster, shorten the TTL itself

ownership-token.name: Ownership token
ownership-token.statement: Renew or release only if the stored token is yours, so an expired holder can't free the next holder's lock.

zombie-release-cascade.name: Zombie release cascade
zombie-release-cascade.statement: An expired holder that still releases frees a live holder's lock, letting more runners pile on.

lock-guards-holders-not-execution.name: A lock guards holders, not execution
lock-guards-holders-not-execution.statement: Deleting a lock key doesn't stop code already running; correctness needs idempotency or fencing, not the lock.

registry-over-switch.name: Registry over switch
registry-over-switch.statement: A per-type registry keeps each type's logic together where a giant switch scatters it.

mapped-type-exhaustiveness.name: Mapped-type exhaustiveness
mapped-type-exhaustiveness.statement: A mapped type over the type union makes a missing registry entry a compile error.

callback-injection-breaks-cycle.name: Injection breaks an import cycle
callback-injection-breaks-cycle.statement: Receiving a function as an argument instead of importing it breaks a circular import.

orphaned-position-record.name: Orphaned position record
orphaned-position-record.statement: Deleting a node leaves contacts' position records pointing at nothing.

forwarding-redirect.name: Forwarding redirect
forwarding-redirect.statement: On delete, leave a redirect from the old node id to a live target.

redirect-chains.name: Redirects chain
redirect-chains.statement: Redirects stack (x→y→z), so resolving a position means following hops.

backward-enumeration.name: Enumerate backward
backward-enumeration.statement: To find contacts affected by deleting Z, enumerate every source whose chain ends at Z, not just records equal to Z.

cascading-delete-set.name: Cascading delete set
cascading-delete-set.statement: A delete can take dependents with it (experiment → variants); affected-contact logic must compose over the whole set.

caller-owned-transaction.name: The caller owns the transaction
caller-owned-transaction.statement: A helper that writes related records takes the caller's tx and never opens its own, so all commit or none do.

throw-rolls-back.name: Throwing is what rolls back
throw-rolls-back.statement: Throwing inside a transaction triggers rollback; returning an error result lets the partial writes commit.

throw-vs-return.name: Throw vs return
throw-vs-return.statement: Expected, user-caused failures return a result; invariant violations and mid-transaction failures throw.

registry-as-decoupling.name: A partial registry as decoupling
registry-as-decoupling.statement: A deliberately partial registry can keep the pure graph model from importing the database layer.

lost-update.name: Lost update
lost-update.statement: Two read-modify-write saves of a whole document race; the second silently clobbers the first.

optimistic-concurrency.name: Optimistic concurrency
optimistic-concurrency.statement: Save only if the version is still the one you read (compare-and-swap); detect the collision at write time instead of locking.

claim-revision-up-front.name: Claim the revision up front
claim-revision-up-front.statement: Claiming the revision first fails fast and takes the row lock, so a concurrent edit blocks, then fails.

redirect-map-keeps-tx-short.name: One map entry keeps the edit short
redirect-map-keeps-tx-short.statement: A delete writes one O(1) redirect entry so the edit transaction stays short; the O(N) bookmark rewrite moves to an async job.

redirect-resolution-walk.name: The resolution walk
redirect-resolution-walk.statement: Resolve by hopping until a live node (success), a repeat (cycle), or nothing (dead end).

load-bearing-waypoint.name: Load-bearing waypoint
load-bearing-waypoint.statement: A middle redirect with no contacts of its own still carries chains through it; cleanup must keep whole chains.

priority-cant-reclaim.name: Priority can't reclaim committed capacity
priority-cant-reclaim.statement: Reactive priority has a ceiling; protecting a class means holding slack in advance.

aimd-asymmetry.name: AIMD asymmetry
aimd-asymmetry.statement: Increase gently, cut sharply; the asymmetry keeps a controller out of the danger zone.

wait-time-signal.name: Control on wait time
wait-time-signal.statement: Steer on wait time against the SLA (end-user impact), not queue length.

atomic-check-and-spend.name: Atomic check-and-spend
atomic-check-and-spend.statement: Checking and spending a shared budget must be one atomic operation, or two spenders both see the last dollar.

bounded-turn-round-robin.name: Bounded-turn round robin
bounded-turn-round-robin.statement: Round robin with bounded turns bounds a tenant's wait by tenant count, not by backlog.

claim-lease-sweep.name: Claim, lease, sweep
claim-lease-sweep.statement: Claiming moves work to an in-progress set stamped with an expiry; a sweeper requeues expired claims.

orthogonal-throttles.name: Two orthogonal throttles
orthogonal-throttles.statement: Class priority (token bucket) and tenant fairness (leases) are independent axes.

common-case-top-level.name: Common case at the top level
common-case-top-level.statement: Make the common case the top-level shape and put variation in optional additive fields, so growth never reshapes the contract.

per-resource-addressing.name: Address each sub-resource
per-resource-addressing.statement: Making each sub-thing its own resource keeps every response a single object; the cost is N+1 fan-out.

counts-not-rates.name: Ship counts, not rates
counts-not-rates.statement: A raw metrics API ships counts; a rate encodes a denominator choice the caller should make.

serve-vs-maintain.name: Expensive to serve vs to maintain
serve-vs-maintain.statement: Costly to keep fresh is not costly to serve: a maintained cache serves instantly.

cache-shared-not-unique.name: Cache what's shared
cache-shared-not-unique.statement: Cache what many requests share; per-request-unique work (arbitrary filters) is what stays expensive to serve.

generator-call-runs-nothing.name: Calling a generator runs nothing
generator-call-runs-nothing.statement: Calling a generator function runs none of its body; the first pull starts it, so a query inside fires on first pull.

yield-freezes-the-frame.name: Yield freezes the frame
yield-freezes-the-frame.statement: A yield mid-loop parks the whole frame, so the row in hand survives to the next pull.

generator-pipeline-stages.name: Stages compose
generator-pipeline-stages.statement: Each stage takes an async iterable and returns one, so stages chain into a pipeline.

fold-needs-grouped-input.name: A fold needs grouped input
fold-needs-grouped-input.statement: A streaming fold assumes rows arrive grouped by key; unsorted input yields several transitions per key.

silent-wrongness-misattribution.name: Silent wrongness misdirects debugging
silent-wrongness-misattribution.statement: A silently wrong result sends you debugging the wrong layer.

editor-ships-buffer.name: The editor ships the buffer
editor-ships-buffer.statement: The editor owns the unsaved buffer, so it must send its contents to the server (didOpen / didChange).

requests-point-at-positions.name: Requests point at positions
requests-point-at-positions.statement: A hover or completion names a position; the server already holds the text.

line-column-edit-locality.name: Line + column survive edits
line-column-edit-locality.statement: Line/column addresses stay valid when text changes elsewhere; flat offsets shift for everything after an edit.

one-checker-two-doors.name: One checker, two doors
one-checker-two-doors.statement: Batch tsc and the language server run the same checker; LSP is a protocol door, not the brain.

translator-hop-cost.name: The translator hop was the cost
translator-hop-cost.statement: The old language server translated every keystroke's request; removing that hop is the speedup.

correlation-tag.name: Correlation tag
correlation-tag.statement: Stamp your own id onto the outgoing mail so SES echoes it back on every event.

durable-row-before-send.name: Durable row before send
durable-row-before-send.statement: The row a tag points to must exist before the send, or a crash leaves the tag pointing at nothing.

raw-ledger-replay.name: Raw ledger enables replay
raw-ledger-replay.statement: Keeping the raw events lets you fix a counting bug and recompute; counters alone are their own only copy.

readers-decoupled.name: Readers are decoupled
readers-decoupled.statement: Each reader of the ledger is its own program, so adding or removing one never touches ingest and one failing doesn't half-finish the others.

cursor-redelivery.name: Crash before bookmark re-reads
cursor-redelivery.statement: A reader that applies effects but dies before saving its bookmark re-reads the same events next tick.

counts-and-bookmark-atomic.name: Effects and bookmark move together
counts-and-bookmark-atomic.statement: Applying effects and moving the bookmark must commit in one transaction.

bookmark-lives-with-effects.name: Bookmark lives with the effects
bookmark-lives-with-effects.statement: With no cross-database transaction, the bookmark lives in the database the reader writes to; reading twice is harmless.

commit-order-not-stamp-order.name: Commit order is not stamp order
commit-order-not-stamp-order.statement: Rows stamped when their insert begins can commit out of order, so a reader can skip past a slow insert forever.

safety-lag.name: Safety lag
safety-lag.statement: Readers only take rows older than now minus X, and X is bounded by the insert's timeout.

retention-slowest-reader.name: Keep from the slowest reader
retention-slowest-reader.statement: Cleanup keeps everything from the oldest reader bookmark onward.

frozen-bookmark-pins-retention.name: A frozen bookmark pins the ledger
frozen-bookmark-pins-retention.statement: A deleted reader's leftover bookmark pins the ledger forever.

no-bookmark-row-means-unborn.name: No row means not born yet
no-bookmark-row-means-unborn.statement: A reader has no bookmark row until its first tick, so a missing row means the reader hasn't run yet.

bookmark-name-contract.name: The bookmark name is a contract
bookmark-name-contract.statement: Retention looks readers up by exact name, so a future reader must write its bookmark under the pre-chosen name or the guard never engages.

sqs-in-flight-invisible.name: Received means hidden, not gone
sqs-in-flight-invisible.statement: ReceiveMessage hides a message for the visibility timeout; only DeleteMessage removes it, otherwise it becomes visible again when the timeout lapses.

sqs-at-least-once.name: At-least-once delivery
sqs-at-least-once.statement: A consumer can finish the work and die (or time out) before DeleteMessage, so any message can be processed more than once; the queue cannot tell 'done but not deleted' from 'never done'.

throw-waits-out-visibility.name: A throw waits out the visibility
throw-waits-out-visibility.statement: A handler that throws (or returns {retry: true}) is not retried immediately: the message is simply not deleted, and it reappears only when its current visibility lapses.

crash-recovery-is-visibility.name: Crash recovery = the visibility timeout
crash-recovery-is-visibility.statement: When a worker dies its extension timer dies with it, so the message reappears at most one visibility timeout after the last receive or extension — the timeout, not the 20s interval, sets recovery time.

visibility-heartbeat.name: The 20s visibility heartbeat
visibility-heartbeat.statement: Loops calls ChangeMessageVisibility every 20s to push the deadline to 30s from now, so a live handler of any length keeps its message with 10s of margin per beat.

visibility-is-not-a-job-timeout.name: Visibility is not a job timeout
visibility-is-not-a-job-timeout.statement: When visibility lapses nothing stops the running handler; the message goes to a second consumer while the first is still working.

receive-count-redrive.name: Receive count and redrive
receive-count-redrive.statement: Every receive bumps the receive count; past maxReceiveCount (3) SQS moves the message to dlq-<queue> — thrown and {retry: true} attempts both count.

timeout-doesnt-cancel-remote.name: A local timeout doesn't cancel the remote
timeout-doesnt-cancel-remote.statement: Giving up on a request on your side doesn't stop the server from committing it, so 'it threw' does not mean 'it didn't happen'.

idempotency-key-minted-before-retry-boun.name: Mint the key outside the outermost retry
idempotency-key-minted-before-retry-boun.statement: A dedupe key only dedupes retries that reuse it, so it must be minted before the outermost retry boundary — at enqueue, carried in the message.

nested-retry-layers.name: Retry layers nest
nested-retry-layers.statement: svix's client retries run inside one SQS delivery, which retries up to 3 receives; each layer dedupes only within the scope where its key was minted.

projection-shards.name: projection shards
projection-shards.statement: Events hash by ses_message_id into 64 fixed shards, each with its own bookmark, so shards project independently.

projection-groups.name: projection groups
projection-groups.statement: A group is one worker's share of the shards (shard % groupCount); bookmarks belong to shards, so changing groupCount moves work without losing progress.

projection-worker-lease.name: projection worker lease
projection-worker-lease.statement: A worker holds a Valkey group lock plus one of two global slots, renewed by heartbeat; busy or full means exit and wait for the next hint.

dispatch-coalescing.name: dispatch coalescing
dispatch-coalescing.statement: At most one queued hint per group: the producer takes an expiring reservation before enqueueing and the worker releases it on success, because a hint carries no data and its copies are pure waste.

pg-is-the-correctness-layer.name: Postgres is the correctness layer
pg-is-the-correctness-layer.statement: Postgres bookmarks and per-shard advisory locks keep the counts right; every Valkey lock above them only avoids wasted or competing work, so losing one costs effort, not correctness.

fence-the-predecessor.name: Fence the old writer before the new ones start
fence-the-predecessor.statement: A writer handoff first proves the old writer has stopped — here by taking its checkpoint lock — or both advance the counts at once.

single-cutoff-start.name: Every shard starts at one cutoff, all at once
single-cutoff-start.statement: All 64 shard bookmarks are created at one cutoff in one transaction; a partial set is refused, because shards started at different points would skip or recount events between them.

cutoff-after-predecessor.name: The new start must be past where the old writer stopped
cutoff-after-predecessor.statement: If the shard cutoff is at or before the global bookmark, events the global writer already counted get counted again, so activation waits instead.

fresh-start-gap.name: A fresh start skips what lies before its cutoff
fresh-start-gap.statement: Shards start at a cutoff one safety lag behind activation, so events after the old writer's last bookmark and before the cutoff are never counted by either writer.

tokens-bound-in-flight.name: Tokens bound work in flight
tokens-bound-in-flight.statement: Debiting a token when an email is scheduled and crediting it when the send completes makes the pool a cap on low-priority emails in flight, not a rate.

credit-exceeds-debit-grows.name: Credit a little more than the debit
credit-exceeds-debit-grows.statement: Each completion returns 1.01 tokens for the 1 it cost, so a healthy pipeline grows its own budget about 1% per turnover; growth is earned only by completions.

every-exit-must-settle.name: Every exit must settle its debit
every-exit-must-settle.statement: Any path that takes a scheduled email out of the pipeline without a completion credit loses its token for good; nothing errors, the pool just shrinks.

recovery-trickle.name: The recovery trickle
recovery-trickle.statement: When the pool is empty and low-priority mail waits, the scheduler adds one token at most once a minute, so the pool can never stay dead but can't refill fast either.

reservation-ledger-refund-once.name: A per-email reservation ledger
reservation-ledger-refund-once.statement: Record each email's debit under its id and delete that entry when it settles, so a replayed failure or a late completion can't return the same token twice.

slow-high-cuts-low.name: A slow high-priority send cuts the low pool
slow-high-cuts-low.statement: A high-priority send that waited past the SLA multiplies the low pool by 0.9; an on-time one adds a hundredth of a token, so low-priority mail yields when the urgent lane slows.

cut-once-per-window.name: One cut per SLA window across workers
cut-once-per-window.statement: Every worker sees the same slowness, so N independent cuts compound to 0.9^N; a shared cooldown key lets exactly one cut land per SLA window.

render-vs-comparison-identity.name: render vs comparison identity
render-vs-comparison-identity.statement: A render is keyed by (tree, frozen recipe, consumed env, renderer contract) and is reusable across branches; a comparison is (before render, after render, frozen expectation) and is what gets judged.

before-is-merge-base-resolved-once.name: before is merge base resolved once
before-is-merge-base-resolved-once.statement: Before is the merge-base of the parent and the tip, with every ref resolved exactly once, so the review diff and the proof consume the same pair even if main moves mid-run.

env-pin-refuses-borrowed-deps.name: env pin refuses borrowed deps
env-pin-refuses-borrowed-deps.statement: Each package the renderer imports must be the exact version the rendered commit lockfile names, checked before execution, else the render is other code wearing this tree name (react 19.3.0 vs 19.3.1 refused).

admission-two-uncached-attempts.name: admission two uncached attempts
admission-two-uncached-attempts.statement: A render identity is trusted only after two independent uncached attempts produce byte-identical scenes; a later fresh mismatch marks it conflicted and nothing reuses it.

machine-checks-declared-invariance.name: machine checks declared invariance
machine-checks-declared-invariance.statement: Each scene is predicted same or changes before rendering; the machine checks the bytes, and any scene whose change disagrees with the prediction is a departure, even if invisible to the eye (#FFFFFF to #FCFCFD).

judgment-carries-on-equal-observation.name: judgment carries on equal observation
judgment-carries-on-equal-observation.statement: A judgment carries to another manifest only when expectation, prediction, scene obligations and every before/after artifact hash are equal; equal pixels under different obligations (a scene captured twice) are not the same observation.

judgment-names-what-was-shown.name: judgment names what was shown
judgment-names-what-was-shown.statement: A verdict names the exact manifest the judge saw; resolving the target at click time lets a different tree receive a verdict nobody gave it (srv/verdicts.py:130 waive).

fire-and-forget-loses-settlement.name: Fire-and-forget loses the settlement
fire-and-forget-loses-settlement.statement: A void-and-catch credit can be dropped when the job finishes or the process exits first, so a settlement that keeps the pool honest must be awaited before the job completes.

release-then-reactivate-strands.name: Release-then-reactivate strands work
release-then-reactivate-strands.statement: Clearing a lease and re-activating the team as separate calls leaves a window where a crash puts the team in neither the active nor the processing set, so no sweeper ever finds its queued mail.

lease-token-fences-completion.name: A claim token fences completion
lease-token-fences-completion.statement: Each claim stores a unique token and completion acts only if the stored token is still its own, so a late or replayed completion cannot release a newer claim on the same team, even one with the same expiry.

drain-before-disconnect.name: Drain before disconnect
drain-before-disconnect.statement: Shutdown stops new ticks and waits for in-flight work before disconnecting its store, under a drain deadline shorter than the kill grace period; whatever does not finish is left as an expiring lease for the sweeper.

cut-leaves-capped-allowance.name: A cut leaves a capped allowance
cut-leaves-capped-allowance.statement: Each applied cut leaves the smaller of 90% of the pool or a fixed 100-email allowance, so a fleet-sized pool drops to a safe level in one cut instead of decaying 10% per window.

repair-only-through-checkpoint.name: Repair only what the projector already passed
repair-only-through-checkpoint.statement: A repair re-applies only skipped events at or before the live projector checkpoint, read under the projector own lock; events past it are still the projector to count, so including them would double-count.

evidence.contrast: maxReceiveCount=3: W1 receives at 0, extends at 20, throws at 25; W2 receives at 50, extends at 70, crashes at 72; W3 polls at 110. Counting extensions says DLQ before W3; right model: W2 sees 2, W3 gets M with count 3.

evidence.note: r6: W2 sees 2 at t=50 (right, ignored the t=20 extension) but then said the t=70 extension bumped M to 3 and dead-lettered it; W3 actually gets M with count 3. Fourth miss; applies the rule inconsistently. Suspect the name ChangeMessageVisibility reads as make-visible/redeliver
evidence.contrast: At t=70 W2 is mid-handler and its timer calls ChangeMessageVisibility(30s): does any worker, W2 included, get M handed to it at that moment? (No: M stays hidden until t=100, so no delivery happens and the count stays 2.)

ses-projection.title: SES event projection
ses-projection.summary: SES delivery events land raw in mail Postgres; readers project them into per-send counters behind a durable bookmark. The sharded version splits the stream into 64 shards worked by leased queue workers (PRs #11092, #11227, #11232, #11234, #11236).

job-queue.title: Job queue (SQS)
job-queue.summary: Background jobs are SQS messages polled by workers (lib/job-queue): delivery is at-least-once, a long job keeps its message by a visibility heartbeat, and 3 receives redrive it to a DLQ. Plan: ~/.dotfiles/learning/plans/sqs-visibility-timeout.md
